statement: A hot-air balloon descends at a steady rate, so its altitude is a linear function of time. The table shows the balloon's altitude $a$, in meters, $t$ minutes after it begins to descend. $$\begin{array}{c|cccc} t & 0 & 4 & 10 & 16 \\ \hline a & 920 & 800 & 620 & 440 \end{array}$$ Which of the following equations models the altitude?

choices.misconception: I used the $120$-meter drop over the first $4$ minutes as the drop per minute, without dividing by $4$.
I divided the change in time by the change in altitude, $\frac{4}{120}$, so I got the reciprocal of the rate.
I found a rate of $30$ meters per minute but made it positive, even though the balloon is going down.

hints: The starting altitude, at $t = 0$, is the constant term. What is the rate of change?
Rate of change $= \frac{\text{change in } a}{\text{change in } t}$. Use any two columns of the table.
From $t = 0$ to $t = 4$, $a$ changes by $800 - 920 = -120$, so the rate is $\frac{-120}{4} = -30$ meters per minute.

solutions.reliable: At $t = 0$ the altitude is $920$, so the constant term is $920$. The rate of change is $\frac{800 - 920}{4 - 0} = -30$ meters per minute, so $a = 920 - 30t$. Check the other columns: $920 - 30 \cdot 10 = 620$ and $920 - 30 \cdot 16 = 440$.
